title: Movement Analysis in Otolaryngology Vertigo Patients and the Effect of Targeted Vestibular Training
summary:
Dizziness can significantly impair a person’s balance, mobility, and quality of life. The causes of dizziness are varied and can affect different parts of the vestibular system. Targeted movement and balance exercises can help alleviate symptoms and improve safety in daily life.

The goal of this study is to investigate changes in mobility and balance in patients with various types of dizziness. To this end, the participants’ movements and balance will first be assessed under the supervision of a physical therapist. The participants will then complete a guided exercise program at home. After completing the training, they will undergo another assessment.

By comparing the examination results, the study aims to determine whether and to what extent movement and balance abilities change as a result of the training, and whether there are differences between the various types of vertigo. In the long term, the results are expected to help make the treatment of vertigo patients more targeted and individualized.
conditions: A wide variety of medical conditions in which patients experience dizziness

interventions.name: Patients aged 14 and older with vertigo of ENT origin are asked to complete a questionnaire (DHI), receive instructions on how to use an app, perform physical therapy exercises at home, and keep a diary regarding their vertigo.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with vertigo caused by ENT conditions (Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, BPLS, vertigo following cochlear implantation) aged 14 and older
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to move or limited mobility due to other pre-existing conditions (e.g., wheelchair, etc.)
